idiom_name: database/sql prepared INSERT in one writer goroutine + timestamp DELETE
implementation_notes: database/sql plus a driver already provides the durable half (transactions, prepared statements, connection pooling), so the pattern reduces to a struct holding one *sql.Stmt and a writer goroutine draining a buffered channel: the classic Store interface and interceptor become a repository and an ordinary background goroutine, and reporting is a read-only query on the same database. Prefer a CGo-free driver such as modernc.org/sqlite so the build stays portable, enable WAL, and keep exactly one writer because SQLite serialises writers and hands SQLITE_BUSY to the loser. Sends into the tap must be non-blocking (select with default, or a bounded buffer whose overflow is counted), and retention is a DELETE on an indexed timestamp column driven by a ticker. The explicit Store abstraction is still justified when several backends or a pluggable reporting schema must be selectable at runtime; otherwise the struct is the whole pattern.
pitfalls: database/sql pools connections, so several goroutines can hold writers at once and SQLite answers with SQLITE_BUSY; pin the writer to one connection (SetMaxOpenConns(1) on the writer handle) and give reports a separate read-only handle.
A blocking channel send re-couples the flow to the store; use select with default (or a bounded buffer) and expose the drop counter, because a full channel must never stall delivery.
*sql.Stmt belongs to the connection that prepared it: a reconnect or a recycled pool entry invalidates it and every later Exec fails until it is re-prepared.
Scanning a BLOB into a []byte can alias driver-owned memory that the next query reuses; copy the bytes before retaining them in a record.
